note: Staging tally for the automated generation-side learner (TD-0035). Owned by .claude/agents/blog-learner.md — it runs after each post's review loops, abstracts that post's ROUND-1 CONFIRMED gate edits (synthesis's gate tier) into content-agnostic patterns, and tallies them across posts. A pattern promotes into docs/blog-drafter-pitfalls.md only at promoteThreshold distinct posts. Health metrics (rounds/tone per post) live here too — they are a SIGNAL, never the optimization target.

patterns.description: Dismiss-then-reframe or 'I don't X, Y does' negation constructions in outline beats and draft prose.
patterns.scope: outline intendedBeat/ourTake fields; draft closing/summary sentences
patterns.note: already covered by blog-drafter-pitfalls.md #1 Negative parallelism — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted

patterns.description: Rule-of-three tricolons (A, B, and C; anaphoric 'its own X, its own Y, its own Z') in lists and prose.
patterns.scope: outline lists; draft prose lists and asides
patterns.note: already covered by blog-drafter-pitfalls.md #2 Rule-of-three tricolons — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted

patterns.description: Outline/draft states a numeric or mechanical fact about our own pipeline (round caps, stage counts, checkpoints) that has drifted from the current value in blog-facts.md.
patterns.scope: outline facts/ourTake fields describing pipeline mechanics
patterns.note: already covered by blog-drafter-pitfalls.md #3 Overclaims about our own pipeline — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted

patterns.description: Links or Sources-lists an internal /blog/<slug>/ whose pubDate is after this post's own pubDate.
patterns.scope: outline links fields; draft body links and Sources section
patterns.note: already covered by blog-drafter-pitfalls.md #4 Future-dated internal links — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted

patterns.description: Outline ourTake reads as flat claim, then cited source, then conclusion, with no personal stake, register, or point of view — a view-from-nowhere failure.
patterns.scope: outline ourTake fields, especially ones citing an external stat or policy

patterns.description: Outline/draft conflates internal pipeline implementation (stages built as narrow agents dispatched via the Agent tool) with the public Skills Marketplace's 'skill' terminology.
patterns.scope: outline facts fields describing pipeline architecture

patterns.description: States an absolute ('the only X', 'always Y') about our own system that a later beat in the same outline itself contradicts with a documented exception.
patterns.scope: outline meta/facts fields making universal claims about pipeline behavior

patterns.description: Closes a sentence or section with 'and that's the whole point' (or equivalent) as a lazy emphasis/summary tag instead of landing the actual point.
patterns.scope: draft synthesis/closing sentences

patterns.description: Reaches for em-dashes by default for asides, contrast, and connectors, pushing draft em-dash density over the tone-gate threshold instead of varying with colons, parens, or sentence breaks.
patterns.scope: draft prose throughout, especially explanatory asides and reviewer/list descriptions

patterns.description: A run of several consecutive sentences — or consecutive list items sharing an identical syntactic frame (e.g. the same colon-tag shape repeated three times) — at a section's emotional or explanatory peak, flattening voice through monotone cadence.
patterns.scope: draft prose, especially mechanism-explanation and emotional-peak sections; draft findings/feature lists

patterns.description: Drops a scope/safety qualifier present in the source claim (e.g., 'AI-audited' collapsed to 'audited') when restating a third-party disclaimed claim, turning a hedged assurance into an unqualified one.
patterns.scope: draft prose citing third-party claims or disclaimers (marketplace audits, vendor claims)
patterns.note: recurring on the marketplace 'audited catalog' phrase specifically — watch for promotion next time it appears

patterns.description: An outline node meant to render as skimmable prose (e.g. a numbered stage rundown, a score list) is left with rendersAsProse set to false, silently dropping the whole beat before it ever reaches the draft.
patterns.scope: outline node fields controlling whether a beat's content reaches the draft
patterns.note: 3 separate beats hit this in the same outline round on grill-me — likely a default-false schema issue, not just a one-off slip; watch for promotion

patterns.description: Closes a paragraph by restating a claim already made in the immediately preceding sentence, in near-identical words, adding no new information — including a short decorative recap fragment that just repeats the prior sentence's point in fewer words.
patterns.scope: draft prose, closing lines of explanatory/mechanism beats

patterns.description: Frames an admitted mistake or an actively-owned pipeline decision in passive or third-person voice (a blog 'ran with' something, 'the orchestrator', 'the loop') instead of Scout's first person, diluting ownership right at the beat meant to carry it.
patterns.scope: draft prose describing self-caught mistakes; outline ourTake/intendedBeat fields personifying pipeline components

patterns.description: Splits a personal cost/admission clause into its own sentence away from the concrete stat or figure it's reacting to, weakening the felt stake the outline called for.
patterns.scope: draft prose pairing a sourced statistic with a personal admission (cost, risk, mistake)

patterns.axis: factual accuracy / grounding claims about our own product
patterns.description: Outline or draft states specific, checkable details about our own product's implementation (pixel measurements, exact UI copy/labels, which visual states change color) confidently, without verifying against the actual source code, and the invented specifics are wrong.
patterns.scope: outline facts/intendedBeat fields and draft prose describing our own product's UI/implementation

patterns.axis: technical honesty / unsupported claim of validation
patterns.description: Outline or draft claims a design choice underwent a formal verification step (e.g. 'colorblind-validated', 'tested', 'audited') when no such process exists anywhere in the codebase or docs — state the design intent/rationale instead of an unearned claim of verification.
patterns.scope: outline facts/intendedBeat fields asserting design rationale for a UI/product choice

patterns.description: Outline or draft cites an external source as backing a specific design/technical choice or trend, but overstates or misstates what that source actually says, conflating the source's own position/framing with a stronger claim we then repeat as fact.
patterns.scope: outline/draft prose citing an external article or guidance to justify a decision or trend claim
patterns.note: grill-me instance: an 'industry is converging on X' claim attributed to a source that actually frames the same facts as attack-chain steps, not an industry trend — watch for promotion

patterns.description: Outline or draft references or links an earlier post of ours — for its current content/state, or as the origin of a feature/decision — without checking what that specific post actually says, producing a misstated current state or misattributed credit.
patterns.scope: outline/draft prose linking to or summarizing an earlier post in this blog

patterns.description: Defines one axis of our own multi-axis scoring/taxonomy system (e.g. AST v1.0's four scores) in a way that folds a deliberately-separate axis back into another, contradicting the spec and undercutting the post's own thesis that the axes are kept apart on purpose.
patterns.scope: outline facts/intendedBeat fields defining our own scoring-system axes

patterns.description: Buries a list of concrete consequences or reach-items inside a single long sentence's trailing subordinate clause instead of giving the list its own short sentence, weakening the payoff of the sentence carrying it.
patterns.scope: draft opening/hook paragraphs stacking a payoff clause with a descriptive list

patterns.description: Compares our own metric to an external stat without checking they measure the same thing (e.g. our confirmed-malicious rate vs. a cited source's broader any-flaw rate), implying an equivalence the underlying denominators don't support.
patterns.scope: outline/draft prose comparing an internal metric to an external benchmark figure

patterns.description: Attributes ownership or authorship of a third-party skill, tool, or example to the researcher/publication that merely studied or cited it, implying they built what they only analyzed.
patterns.scope: draft prose citing third-party research examples
